item.title: Tuen Mun knife suspect shot dead may have been under drug influence, Hong Kong police say
item.description: A man shot dead by officers at a Tuen Mun shopping mall on Thursday night, after he wielded a 30-centimetre knife and held a woman captive, may have been under the influence of drugs, Hong Kong police have said. item.title: 3.2% economic growth in 2025 despite low consumption, Hong Kong finance chief says
item.description: Hong Kong saw an increase in economic growth of 3.2 per cent last year, Hong Kong’s finance chief has said, although consumption remained low. item.title: China protests over Philippine coast guard’s President Xi images
item.description: The Chinese Embassy in Manila said Friday it has filed a diplomatic protest against a Philippine Coast Guard spokesman over a social media post that included cartoonish images of President Xi Jinping. item.title: Hong Kong construction industry body distributes 3,000 flame-retardant scaffold nets
item.description: A statutory body representing Hong Kong’s construction industry has begun distributing fire-retardant scaffolding nets to 19 renovation sites, after maintenance projects across the city were suspended in the wake of the deadly fire in Tai Po. item.description: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed on a raft of measures from trade to tourism on Friday at the first meeting between the countries’ leaders in Beijing in eight years.
